To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) TLS is a viable technique for parallelizing programs that have a large number of threads and (ii) data dependence speculation is the most effective form of TLS.

(1) TLS can be applied to only 2.4% of the loops in SPEC CPU2006, (2) the upper-bound on speedup for TLS in SPEC CINT2005 and CFP2005 is of the order 1%, (3) the upper-bound for TLS is limited by the threading overhead and (4) the misspeculation penalty is not a significant factor.

(a) for the SPEC CINT20006 suite, the unique performance potential of TLS is of the order 1% at the loop level, (b) for the SPEC CF2006 suite, the unique potential of TLS is 2% at the loop-level, and (c) the performance of the various types of thread speculation is very similar to each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: "How much performance potential does TLS offer for SPEC CPU 2006?"
the following question: What is the maximum performance gain that one can expect from TLS?
a tight performance analysis of thread speculation, and is not a performance evaluation of TLS in general.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance potential of TLS is very small and is limited to the order of 10% for the whole benchmark.
, at this point, TLS has little potential to improve the performance of SPEC CPU2006.
TLS is a technique that has a very limited potential for performance improvement in the context of SPEC CPU2006.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TLS is not a viable technique to parallelize ordinary serial codes.
TLS, at the inner most loop level, is a very weak form of speculation.
, at the loop level, TLS is not a viable option for performance enhancement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TLS, in general, and the specific forms of TLS, viz., control and data value speculations, in particular, are unlikely to be the key enablers of multi-core performance in the foreseeable future.
the performance of TLS is limited by a number of real-world factors, and hence the reported speedups in the literature are not indicative of the true potential of this technique.
, in the absence of any special hardware support, TLS is unlikely to be useful for parallelization of ordinary serial programs. © 2008 IEEE.
